# HarnessDock v0.1.6-alpha.2

HarnessDock `v0.1.6-alpha.2` aligns the sealed desktop Runtime with DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2` and closes two release-critical lifecycle gaps: lingering Node descendants after client exit and stale plugin quarantine crossing Runtime upgrades.

This is a **replaceable prerelease**. Stable `v0.1.5` remains immutable. Publication is allowed only from one exact main SHA after the source, candidate, packaged-startup, Runtime identity, and checksum gates pass.

## Upstream alignment

- Runtime tag: `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2`
- Runtime commit: `ddefc45fbc7f8e46dd73185e68295696d1297887`
- HarnessDock base version remains `0.1.6`; candidate identity advances to `v0.1.6-alpha.2`.
- Upstream alpha.2 adds the Plugins management surface with live enable/disable, runtime plugin dependency resolution/unloading, improved CLI/Web startup latency, the `dsh <profile>` shorthand, and multi-instance Session changes.
- HarnessDock keeps the existing `--profile <name>` launcher spelling because upstream explicitly maps the shorthand to the same profile-selection path.
- Desktop targets continue to seal the official upstream Git source closure. Android/iOS remain Remote Gateway-only clients.

## Plugin isolation hardening

- Persisted quarantine is upgraded to schema v4 and is valid only for the exact dsh version, sealed Runtime image identity, and launch scope.
- A quarantine learned on `0.1.6-alpha.1` cannot silently disable plugin rows after upgrading to `0.1.6-alpha.2`.
- Automatic quarantine continues to use the upstream-supported id-targeted `disabled: true` overlay.
- Explicit Rescue Web still starts the shipped Web profile in a generation-private `DSH_HOME`, so user plugin state, profile healing, caches, or writer locks cannot block recovery.
- The required Windows packaged-startup gate now injects a broken third-party plugin and requires automatic quarantine to disable it and recover to healthy Harness Web.

## No-orphan shutdown hardening

- Registered process cleanup now terminates the rooted process tree while the direct parent PID is still valid, reaps the parent, then performs a final Windows Job Object / POSIX process-group cleanup.
- This closes the Windows spawn-to-Job assignment escape window without targeting a possibly reused parent PID after exit.
- Runtime startup failure, cancellation, config-dump timeout, restart, normal close, tray quit, and final app teardown share the same ownership cleanup primitive.
- Windows installed smoke additionally snapshots pre-existing Node processes and requires the post-launch Node delta to be zero after a normal `CloseMainWindow()` exit.

## Release gates

The exact candidate SHA must pass repository checks, Rust/Tauri checks, parity contracts, full sealed Runtime packaging, installed Windows normal startup, private Rescue startup under writer-lock contention, broken-plugin quarantine recovery, same-SHA release gates, Runtime identity verification, and `SHA256SUMS` verification before publication.
